concerns.text: The plan states for Deep Ensembles: 'Aleatoric: Mean of the 5 predicted variances (if model outputs variance) or estimated via residual analysis'. The baseline FFNN (FR-002) is defined as a standard MSE regressor which outputs a single point estimate, not a variance. Without modifying the baseline architecture to output variance (e.g., heteroscedastic loss) or explicitly defining the residual analysis procedure on the test set, the 'Aleatoric' component cannot be calculated as described. This breaks the FR-008 requirement to separate uncertainty types.

The plan proposes using McNemar's test for the downstream screening comparison (US-3). McNemar's test is designed for paired nominal data (2x2 contingency tables) to compare classification accuracy. The screening task involves comparing 'precision at fixed recall' (a continuous metric derived from ranking/filtering) between two methods. Using McNemar's test here is statistically invalid; a paired t-test on precision scores across multiple bootstrap samples or a permutation test on the precision difference is required to validly claim significance.

The plan specifies 'Stratified Split by Quantiles' for the 80/10/10 split. While this ensures distributional similarity, it does not account for the 'MaterialSample' entity structure if the dataset contains multiple entries per material (e.g., different phases or calculations). If the raw OQMD subset has duplicates or correlated samples, a random/quantile split will cause data leakage (training on a sample and testing on its duplicate), artificially inflating calibration metrics (ECE) and invalidating the causal claim that the UQ method is robust.
